description: Quick mix of several soundfiles, all starting at time zero, with AUTOMATIC PEAK NORMALISATION: a first pass ('INFO: Finding maximum level') measures the summed mix's peak, then every input gets the SAME gain so the output peaks at full scale. Verified in BOTH directions: three overlapping full-level copies (raw sum peak 2.970) rendered at gain 0.33669 each, output peak 0.99997 - no wrap, no clip; and two QUIET files (raw sum peak 0.216) were amplified to output peak 1.0000. There are NO parameters at all. Output duration = the longest input, sample-exact (3.0 from 1+2+3 s; 2.0 from a pair). All inputs must share one channel count ('ERROR: INVALID DATA / ERROR: Incompatible channel-count in input file <name>.') and one sample rate ('...Incompatible sample-rate in input file <name>.'). This entry pins THREE inputs (the mode's 'several' point - two-file jobs belong to submix merge); the binary is variadic (a 2-file run verified) - use execute() for other counts. Deterministic (identical decoded shas 1.2 s apart).
musical_use: The instant vertical stack: audition chords of processed variants, pile sweep() outputs into a cluster, or check how N layers sit together - without writing a mixfile and without any headroom arithmetic, because the normalisation pass makes overload impossible. The tradeoff is absolute level: the output ALWAYS peaks at full scale, so a stack of whispers comes out as loud as a stack of roars (relative balance BETWEEN the files is preserved - single shared gain). That makes mergemany ideal for material you will re-level downstream and wrong for anything whose absolute quietness matters (re-attenuate with modify loudness afterwards, or use submix mix with explicit levels). All sounds start at 0: for timed entries use submix mix; for two files with offset/skew control use submix merge.

examples.description: Stack three processed variants of one source into a normalised cluster.
examples.expected_use: Pass exactly three references; output = the longest input's duration, peak-normalised to full scale regardless of input levels.

known_issues: ALWAYS NORMALISES TO FULL SCALE, in both directions (first-class behavior): hot sums are scaled down (3x full-level -> per-file gain 0.33669, peak 0.99997) and quiet sums are scaled UP (sum peak 0.216 -> output peak 1.0000). Relative balance between the inputs is preserved (one shared gain), absolute level is not. Never rely on it to keep quiet material quiet.
Overload-proof by construction - the safe many-file counterpart to submix mix's WRAP. No getlevel pre-flight needed.
All inputs start at time zero and there are no parameters - no offsets, no levels, no pans. Reach for submix mix the moment you need any of those.
Channel counts must all match (refusal verbatim, names the offending file) and sample rates must all match (ditto). A stereo trio renders stereo (verified).
This entry pins input_arity 3; the binary accepts 2 or more (2-file run verified). For 4+ files use execute() - or submix mix, which scales to hundreds of events.
Multi-input entry: duration rule (indur_max) verified at 3 and 2 inputs in docs/curation/tranche12_submix_depth.md; duration_row null (tranche-11 rule).
